payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to suppress electrolyte crossover, a principal aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. Independent auditing established the governing cycle life at 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold; the earlier 12,000-cycle claim was retracted because it used un-normalized depth of discharge. The prototype’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. At projected 500 MWh-scale manufacturing, its stack-level cost is $61/kWh. The chemistry cannot operate below 4 °C because the thalliline dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte.
